prompt: What is the role of the moderator in a nuclear reactor?
options: To reduce the kinetic energy of neutrons
To transfer thermal energy to the turbines
markscheme: **B.** The moderator slows neutrons so they are more likely to cause fission of U-235.

prompt:
Each fission of uranium-235 releases about $200\ \text{MeV}$. A reactor produces a thermal power of $3.0\ \text{GW}$.

**(a)** Calculate the number of fissions per second. **[2]**

**(b)** Determine the mass of U-235 used per day. (Mass of one U-235 atom $= 3.9 \times 10^{-25}\ \text{kg}$.) **[2]**

**(c)** Explain why control rods are needed and how they keep the power constant. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $200\ \text{MeV} = 200\times10^6\times1.6\times10^{-19} = 3.2\times10^{-11}\ \text{J}$ ✓; $\tfrac{3.0\times10^9}{3.2\times10^{-11}} = 9.4\times10^{19}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ ✓

**(b)** Fissions per day $= 9.4\times10^{19}\times86400 = 8.1\times10^{24}$ ✓; mass $= 8.1\times10^{24}\times3.9\times10^{-25} \approx 3.2\ \text{kg}$ ✓

**(c)** Each fission releases more than one neutron, so without control the rate would grow ✓; the rods absorb neutrons and are adjusted so that on average exactly one neutron per fission causes a further fission ✓
